solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two companies beginning to advertise drink

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, taken twice

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pair of firms jointly launch an advertising campaign for a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: CO for company is a crossword staple; doubling it gives the first four letters at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans mixed with milk or water.

clue.text: Family close to deafening loud noise

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Relatives gathered near some ear-splitting racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near' in the surface, but here it means the closing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a resonant metallic sound, such as a bell or struck pan makes.

clue.text: I'm so confused with clue for amphitheatre

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up and must be put back in a sensible order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
'with' adds this word to the letters already gathered

explanation.surface: A baffled solver admits being lost over a clue whose answer is an arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' looks like an intensifier for 'confused', but its letters belong in the mix: I'M + SO + CLUE together make the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coliseum (Colosseum) in Rome is the most famous ancient amphitheatre, and the word also names any large stadium.

indicators.note: something going wrong falls out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken together as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A commander laments that the offensive is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alas' and 'is' read as a sigh in the surface, but they are just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently, a direct synonym for launching an assault.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to strike repeatedly and hard
second meaning: the one who swings at the pitch, 'perhaps' because cricketers bat too

explanation.surface: Someone wants to beat up a ballplayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals the second meaning is one example of a wider class of people who bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means hitting something repeatedly, and the noun names whoever holds the bat at the plate.

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so the word is taken by ear rather than spelling

parts.note: the person who adjusts a piano's strings to pitch

explanation.surface: The man who came to tune the piano landed a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the final R is silent, so the technician's title and the fish sound identical. 'Caught' suits the fish so well it hides its job as the hearing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, widely eaten fresh or tinned.

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a place is a position or spot

explanation.surface: A sports team swaps in a player who has a very unusual role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely rare' reads as 'very rare' but means the extreme letters of rare.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute something is to put another in its stead, exactly what replacing it means.

clue.text: Certain about one insect's identifying mark

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the others

parts.note: sure means certain
the Roman numeral for one
a gnat is a small flying insect; the 's is just possessive

explanation.surface: Someone is confident they can spot a bug's distinguishing feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect's' looks possessive, tying the mark to the bug, but the 's simply ends the word; 'about' wraps the certain word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's handwritten name, used as a personal mark that authenticates documents.

clue.text: Old conqueror — he hangs king, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go awry, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: the three words together supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A ruthless warlord of history executes a monarch, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one grim historical sentence; the dash separates the definition from the rearranged words.
explanation.definitionFit: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire in the thirteenth century, conquering vast stretches of Asia.

clue.text: A condiment knocked over reference book

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up lying the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: salt is a basic table condiment

explanation.surface: A cellar of seasoning gets spilled on a book at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the condiment flips; the A stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, consulted as a geographical reference work.

parts.note: income after deductions is net
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Once the taxes are paid, it's time to celebrate and play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a position instruction but belongs to the phrase meaning net pay. Netball is a British court sport like basketball, mostly played by women and girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport in which players pass a ball and shoot into a high ring, so a sport or game.

clue.text: Leave with first aid device for young bird

parts.note: to go is to leave
a sling supports an injured arm; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: A rescued chick is sent off with a bandage support.
explanation.walkthrough: A sling is the cloth support that holds an injured arm, standard first aid kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a baby goose, the young of a waterfowl.

clue.text: Unorthodox thinker's quote recalled by that woman

parts.note: her is the pronoun for that woman

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word comes back the way it went

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A woman remembers a saying by a radical philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. 'By' puts the woman's pronoun beside the flipped quote.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds beliefs contrary to established doctrine, a person whose thinking departs from orthodoxy.

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: then means afterwards
a rave is a glowing review

explanation.surface: A poem later earns rapturous acclaim from critics.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (3,5) hides the split: the outer word breaks after its third letter, so the result reads as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raven is Edgar Allan Poe's famous 1845 poem about a talking bird, so a specific example of a poem.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of the word
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Trying to revive a friend who has been knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: MATE is everyday British for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring life or energy to something, just as enlivening does.

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone feels a growing awareness of a mortal enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'm is ignored; its two letters join the five of 'sense'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an arch-enemy or long-standing rival who seems destined to bring about one's downfall.

clue.text: Quickly write introduction of symphony's slow movement

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the very start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: opening letter of the word
a crawl is a slow way of moving

explanation.surface: A composer dashes off the opening of a symphony's adagio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' sounds like a musical term, but it is just a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to write hurriedly and untidily, so jotting something fast and carelessly.

indicators.note: inside points to letters lying within the following words

parts.note: letters run across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Things are normally kept safe within the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the comma: the last four letters of 'ranch' and the first two of 'ordinarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: To anchor is to fix firmly in place, the verb sense of making something secure.

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
red is wine of that colour

explanation.surface: Choosing a bottle to serve the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning type.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred is a collective noun for a person's blood family and kin.

clue.text: Fool covered at first in pile of sand

indicators.note: in places one element within another

parts.note: a dune is a sandy mound

indicators.note: at first points to the very start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A silly person ends up buried in a sandheap on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered' sounds like the sand burying the fool, but only its first letter is used, slotted into the dune before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, traditionally made to wear a pointed cap at school.

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so one word bears another within

parts.note: a march is a parade
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal procession continues on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' looks like a single phrase meaning continuing; split it into the container signal and the word held.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a king or queen, a sovereign head of state.

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of the following words

parts.note: letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A scientist says the research calls for a bit of genetic modification.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the last two letters of 'gene' and the first two of 'editing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to have a requirement for it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Safe place to eat starter of nigiri

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A restaurant recommendation: a secure spot for sushi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests an appetiser, fitting the meal, but here it means first letter. Nigiri is a type of sushi.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a refuge or sanctuary, originally a harbour sheltering ships.

clue.text: Rough wood taken for martial art

indicators.note: rough means crude or unpolished, so the letters need working into proper shape

parts.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Splintery planks used in a combat-sport demonstration, perhaps for breaking with a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' reads as describing the wood but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean combat discipline known for kicks, one of the recognised fighting arts.

indicators.note: most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a ranger patrols and looks after a forest

explanation.surface: A woodland warden owns most of a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: RANGER loses its last letter. The 's means 'is', linking wordplay to definition rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove with several hotplates and an oven, as in a kitchen range.
